expansion incase you couldnt get the doc:

[spoiler]

Foreston, New Texas 1/1/2012

	Sir, we need to escort you out of the city! screeches one of president Hozumis personal bodyguards from a radio, Most exits are backed by people, and this building will inevitably be breached. We, and especially you, dont want to be near this building or in this city when that happens. I will call multiple police stations and tell them to escort us out of the city. No, do not do that. That will only alert more people, and the nearest stations are about one hour out anyway. We can make it out by going through the furthest exit from the main entrance, and hijacking a car to escape. It is night, so we could escape almost like wed never been here. replies another guard on the radio, for the screams and yells of the mob just outside were too loud for regular talk. The capitol building was engulfed by angry citizens. Everywhere seemed to be blocked by protestors, and many hundreds of Areneese people living there either evacuated, or hid. It seemed as if New arenenge was on a verge of civil war, as protestors were raiding buildings, and some even injured government officials. The Circle (New Arenenges Pentagon) has contacted the military to help Foreston out, but most bases were very far out, so it would take at least a day for the army to get to the capitol. Until then, the handful of bodyguards were to sort things out with the president. 

Zion county, Benim 1/2/1022

	The president had successfully escaped the capitol, which was overrun by very harsh and demanding protestors. A few hours later at dawn they arrived at a long state border, which meant they were safe for now, and away from the capitol's state: Unimah. After driving to the window, one of the officers glanced at the car, and then the people inside. He jumped at the sight of a dusty president and his bodyguards waiting for him to open the gate. The officer quickly gave them a map and a fairly large and dark bag with necessities, because he knew about the mass protesting and that the president wasn't safe. The security conveniently had an armoured car next to the gate, to which the president quickly hopped inside of. After a short talk, and a couple handshakes, the armoured car sped out of sight into the other state. After the president had gone, one of the security personnel hesitantly called the borders manager and told him of the weird scenario that just happened. The president just came through here! He said, You sure the president of New Arenenge has come through THIS border? It does make sense because this is the fastest route out of state from Foreston, where Hozumi was previously at. Alright, and? And? He replied,  I just thought it would be cool to tell you that I met the president in person and you didn't. What? Bragging isn't cool, and you really think I care about seeing the president in person? Is he still here? No. There was a moment of silence in the call, and the manager sighed. Alright, bye, and do NOT call me back- He had hung up. Jeez I really hate that guy. He thinks hes better than the president. 

Kamimna County, Ferska | Three Weeks Later

	The group has finally reached the Circle, and the capitol had been cooled. All of the heads of departments and ministers gathered in a room to discuss what happens next. Some of the council discussed an apology for the nation, and accepting the terms of the people. But most people disagreed, stating that they don't want an apology, they want action. So what should we do then? Asks the head of the Dept. of State, Like I said, ACTION. The people won't find our apology sincere, and some might even disagree with what we say in it. Answers the Head of the Dept. of Labor, We should just make them happy by doing what they want us to do. We know what they want us to do. President Hozumi, your term is almost over, in fact, it ends this month! They elected an expansionist guy for Christs sake! SO we should just go ahead and do that. Hozumi thought about it, and thought about it again. After a while of staring at the papers, and clenching his hands, he, and every department head in the large, dim room hesitantly, but inevitably passed the expansion. A few days later, the recruitment camp had so many people that they had to stop recruiting. About 29,000 people signed up for the expansion groups, but only about 8,000 passed.  Many groups were sent out to fulfill that expansion in hopes that the unrest will go down, and the protests will stop. [/spoiler]
